exercise.name: Dumbbell Lying Woodchop

reference.title: Dumbbell Lying Woodchop
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (trunk flexion with rotation, shoulder extension)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl up and chop across, breathe in as you lower back down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbell; light to moderate, held by the ends
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a heavier dumbbell; slower lowering

cues.text: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Hold the dumbbell by its ends with straight arms above the head, off to the left side, a little off the floor.
Breathe out, curl the head and shoulders up and turn to the right, sweeping the dumbbell in an arc over the body to the outside of the right knee.
Pause with the right shoulder blade off the floor and the left shoulder turned toward the right knee.
Breathe in and reverse the arc slowly, lowering the trunk and taking the dumbbell back above the head to the left.
Rest the shoulders, keep the dumbbell off the floor, and repeat.

mistakes.fix: Lead with the ribs: curl and turn the trunk, the arms stay long.
Keep the feet flat and heavy on the floor.
Keep a fist of space between chin and chest; the neck follows the trunk.
Lower for about two seconds and stop a little off the floor.

kinematics.norm: Head, shoulders and shoulder blades curl off the floor, as in a twisting crunch (clinical opinion); curl-up and oblique crunch variations load the obliques and rectus abdominis (Escamilla 2006)
Turn toward the knee about 20-30 degrees, mostly thoracic (clinical opinion)
Diagonal arc from above the opposite shoulder to outside the knee (clinical opinion)
Feet flat, pelvis on the floor (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #14495, Dumbbell Lying Woodchop, video (movement reference only; page not read)
Escamilla et al. 2006, electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training (Phys Ther 86(5):656-671; PubMed 16649890)
Konrad, Schmitz and Denner 2001, neuromuscular evaluation of trunk-training exercises (J Athl Train 36(2):109-118; PMC155519)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Repeated loaded trunk flexion with rotation stresses the discs; skip it with a disc problem or back pain (McGill 1998).
Keep the dumbbell light enough to control over the face.
modify: Back discomfort: smaller curl, no dumbbell.
Shoulder discomfort overhead: start with the dumbbell above the chest instead of above the head.
regressions: Lighter dumbbell or a medicine ball.

muscleNotes.obliques_l: Prime movers: rotate and flex the trunk toward the right knee (left external with right internal oblique).
